title: Animals on the Hour  - Time to the Hour Read Aloud Math Analog Clock Animals
ss_wr_desc: Introduce children to time-related vocabulary through daily routines and visual timetables. Encourage use of terms like "before", "after", "first", "next", "finally", "morning", "afternoon", "evening" to describe and order events. Utilise storybooks to contextualise these concepts in different scenarios.
small_step_id: Year 1_5-6_Summer__Time_1_Before and after, preposition time words

title: Around the Clock with Harriet - Read Aloud Time on the Hour
ss_wr_desc: Children learn to tell time using an analogue clock, understanding "o'clock" and viewing the clock face as a number line. They start by reading the hour hand, then progress to the minute hand, learning the difference in length. They know to check the shorter hand when the minute hand points to 12.
small_step_id: Year 1_5-6_Summer__Time_5_Tell the time to the hour

title: Eggs and Legs Counting by Twos - (Read Aloud)
ss_wr_desc: Build on children's understanding of adding 1 and 2, doubles, and finding 1 more/less by exploring counting in 2s, using pairs like socks or bicycle wheels. Use number lines and a 1-50 grid to spot patterns. Introduce multiplication language, always starting from even numbers.

title: From the Garden: A Counting Book About Growing Food
ss_wr_desc: This step aims to enable children to count to 10 fluently and accurately, applying five counting principles: one-to-one assignment, stable-order, cardinality (final object equals total count), abstraction (counting intangible things like sounds), and order-irrelevance (counting order doesn't change total).

title: Give Me Half! - Read Aloud Math Book
ss_wr_desc: Teach doubling and halving numbers using concrete resources and pictures. Clarify misconceptions like doubling means adding 2. Once students understand, encourage pattern recognition and prediction, such as "If I know double 2, I can find double 20". Explore halving odd numbers with concrete resources.

title: Hands Down Counting by Fives 5's - Read Aloud
ss_wr_desc: Children learn to count in 5s using various methods like starfish arms, dice, rhymes, and ten frames. They practice orally to solidify this skill. The 1-50 grid helps identify patterns in counting by 5s. The language of multiplication, such as "equal groups of 5," is introduced.

title: Jack the Builder - Counting on Math (Read Aloud)
ss_wr_desc: Count from any number up to 10, using tools like ten frames and number tracks for support. These tools link numerals and words, aiding understanding. Avoid number lines at this stage to prevent confusion. This counting skill is crucial for preparing children for addition.
small_step_id: Year 1_5-6_Autumn__Place value within 10_6_Count on from any number

title: Leaping Lizards / Skip Counting - A Read Aloud Math Book
ss_wr_desc: Year 1 students review counting in 2s, 5s, and 10s, both forwards and backwards, preparing for topics like money. Starting numbers for 2s and 5s should be multiples. Counting in 10s can start from any number. Concrete resources like counters and Rekenreks aid understanding. Spotting patterns in numbers is encouraged.

title: Lots of Ladybugs Counting by Fives - Read Aloud with Skip Counting
ss_wr_desc: Focus on the 5 times-table, including zero, to understand multiplication and division by 5. Use multiple representations and manipulatives to support learning. Encourage efficient counting strategies, spotting patterns, and making connections with the 10 times-table. Reinforce knowledge of 5 times-table facts throughout.

title: Plenty of Petals Counting by Tens - (Read Aloud)
ss_wr_desc: Children focus on the 10 times-table, counting forwards and backwards in 10s, and explore division by 10. They use various representations like number tracks, lines, and bar models, and draw images to match number sentences. Base 10 supports understanding. Links between 10 and 5 times-tables are explored later.

title: Toasty Toes Counting by Tens - (Read Aloud)
ss_wr_desc: Explore the 5 and 10 times-tables, understanding their relationship and identifying common numbers. Recognise that all numbers in the 10 times-table appear in the 5 times-table, but not vice versa. Learn that the 10 times-table is double the 5 times-table, exemplified by 4x10 equalling 8x5.

title: Adding & Subtracting! | Mini Math Movies | Scratch Garden
ss_wr_desc: Formalise addition as combining parts to form a whole. Focus on uniting two parts, using correct mathematical language like "is equal to". Use ten frames, counters, Rekenreks, and part-whole models to represent additions. This foundational concept supports later learning and builds on previous knowledge.
small_step_id: Year 1_5-6_Autumn__Addition and subtraction within 10_8_Addition – add together

title: Composing Numbers & Decomposing Numbers! | Mini Math Movies | Scratch Garden
ss_wr_desc: Introduce the language of "parts" and "whole" to children, reinforcing prior knowledge. Facilitate exploration of number compositions, such as 5 being 2 and 3, or 1 and 4. Encourage recognition that numbers can be composed of multiple parts. Promote understanding through play and physical activities. Introduce part-whole model next.
small_step_id: Year 1_5-6_Autumn__Addition and subtraction within 10_1_Introduce parts and wholes

title: Counting Odd Numbers | Counting Songs | Scratch Garden
ss_wr_desc: Children explore odd and even numbers, identifying if a number is odd or even through representations like number pieces. They learn that even numbers can be halved into two equal parts, while odd numbers cannot. Understanding secure, they check the ones column to determine a number's oddness or evenness.
small_step_id: Year 2_6-7_Spring__Multiplication and division_12_Odd and even numbers

title: Counting by Quarters | Counting Songs | Scratch Garden
ss_wr_desc: Children learn to count in 50s, using their knowledge of the 5 times-table. They understand that each number in 50s is 10 times larger than in 5s. They practice counting forwards and backwards from any multiple of 50 up to 1,000. Number lines, tracks, and real-life contexts like money and measures aid learning.

title: Counting! | Mini Math Movies | Scratch Garden
ss_wr_desc: Learn to symbolise real-life objects like apples or sweets with counters and cubes, matching numerals to objects. Understand that anything can be represented and counted with maths tools or images. Practice writing numerals corresponding to object sets, using ten frames for structured organisation of manipulatives.

title: Data! | Mini Math Movies | Scratch Garden
ss_wr_desc: In this section, children learn statistics and data representation using tally charts. They understand number representation, use a "gate" for groups of 5, and count in 5s to total tallies. Once confident, they draw their own tallies to record object numbers. Mastery of tallies is essential before progressing.

title: Data! | Mini Math Movies | Scratch Garden
ss_wr_desc: Interpret and construct pictograms, extending Year 2 knowledge. Ask and answer questions about data in horizontal and vertical pictograms. Understand symbol values, including half, quarter, and three-quarter symbols. Recognise the importance of the key in interpreting data. Reflect on symbol choice and its data relationship.

title: Estimating! | Mini Math Movies | Scratch Garden
ss_wr_desc: Children learn to estimate, initially on a number line, exploring the halfway point and using informal measurements for verification. They discuss with peers to understand estimation, overcoming the challenge of inexact answers. Confidence in using a number line is crucial, for instance, reasoning that 4 is less than halfway on a 0-10 line.
small_step_id: Year 1_5-6_Spring__Place value within 20_10_Estimate on a number line to 20

title: Fractions! | Mini Math Movies | Scratch Garden
ss_wr_desc: Children should explore and identify halves using various objects and shapes. They need practical experience and diverse representations to understand that a half means "one of two equal parts". They should recognise when a shape or object is or isn't a half, without using fractional notation.
small_step_id: Year 1_5-6_Summer__Fractions_1_Recognise a half of an object or a shape

title: Location & Directions! | Mini Math Movies | Scratch Garden
ss_wr_desc: Children learn terms "full", "half", "quarter", and "three-quarter" for turns, applying them practically to objects and shapes. They identify turn size by comparing starting and ending positions, and explore if different turns yield the same direction. This reinforces learning on 2-D and 3-D shapes.

title: Measuring! | Mini Math Movies | Scratch Garden
ss_wr_desc: Children begin measuring object lengths and heights using consistent non-standard units like cubes or paper clips. They understand the importance of using equal-sized units for accurate measurements and comparisons. Previous learning is reinforced as they compare lengths measured with the same unit.
small_step_id: Year 1_5-6_Spring__Length and height_2_Measure length using objects

title: Patterns! | Mini Math Movies | Scratch Garden
ss_wr_desc: Explore shape patterns, including turns. Recap simple patterns before introducing patterns with turns. Identify next shapes and their direction. Use terms like quarter, half, three-quarter turns, clockwise, and anticlockwise. Discuss full turns in pattern creation. Practice with cut-out shapes before describing patterns.
small_step_id: Year 2_6-7_Summer__Position and direction_5_Shape patterns with turns

title: Probability! | Mini Math Movies | Scratch Garden
ss_wr_desc: Updated May 2026

title: Shapes! | Mini Math Movies | Scratch Garden
ss_wr_desc: Children sort 2-D shapes based on properties like type, size, and colour. They identify how shapes are grouped, discuss similarities and differences, and understand that orientation doesn't change a shape's properties. Exploration of similarities between squares and rectangles is encouraged.

title: The Counting Down from 100 Song | Counting Songs | Scratch Garden
ss_wr_desc: Practise counting to 100, building on place value knowledge up to 50. Explore oral counting of numbers 50-100, forwards and backwards, to recognise patterns. Count objects to understand quantity. Use hundred squares to link numerals with number names, reinforcing the concept of "how many?"

title: The Counting Down from 20 Song | Counting Songs | Scratch Garden
ss_wr_desc: In the Autumn term, children progress from learning numbers up to 10 to counting to 20. Regular verbal counting exercises, such as tallying students or objects, aid this. Understanding teen numbers can be challenging due to their irregular pattern, but concrete resources and number tracks can help visualise their "10-and-a-bit" structure. "I count, you count" activities reinforce counting from various starting points.

title: The Counting by Eights Song | Counting Songs | Scratch Garden
ss_wr_desc: Children deepen their understanding of the 8 times-table by multiplying and dividing by 8, using arrays and partitioning (e.g., 7x8 = 5x8 + 2x8). They explore commutativity (3x8 = 8x3) and find numbers greater than 96 in the 8 times-table using partitioning (e.g., 10x8 + 6x8 = 128).

title: The Counting by Fours Song | Counting Songs | Scratch Garden
ss_wr_desc: Leverage knowledge of the 2 times-table to multiply by 4 using arrays and doubling. Link the 4 and 5 times-tables, understanding that 4x7 equals 5x7 minus 7. Apply equal groups concept, using concrete and pictorial representations to connect counting in 4s and multiplying by 4. Explore multiplication's commutativity.

title: The Counting by Hundreds Song | Counting Songs | Scratch Garden
ss_wr_desc: In Year 2, children learn to count in 100s, understanding that 10 tens equal 1 hundred, and 100 is 10 times larger than 10. They explore multiples of 100 within 1,000 and identify tens in any 3-digit multiple of 100. Base 10 supports this learning process.

title: The Counting by Tens Song | Counting Songs | Scratch Garden
ss_wr_desc: Build on children's understanding of counting in 10s up to 50 using ten frames, straws, bead strings, and number grids. Introduce multiplication language without the symbol until Year 2. Focus on multiples up to 50, then explore counting from non-multiples of 10 like 42, 32, 22, 12, 2.

title: The Counting by Threes Song | Counting Songs | Scratch Garden
ss_wr_desc: Children learn to count in 3s using concrete resources and identify patterns. They solve problems abstractly with number lines, number tracks, or hundred squares. Techniques assist with crossing a 10 boundary. By the end, they should count forwards and backwards from any multiple of 3 and spot sequence errors.

title: The Directions Song | The North South East West Song | Scratch Garden
ss_wr_desc: Children learn to describe positions using "forwards" and "backwards", initially through physical movement. Instructions progress to specific steps, like "3 steps forwards". This understanding is reinforced through games and pre-programmable toys. Once confident, they combine "left" and "right" with these terms for complex movements.
small_step_id: Year 1_5-6_Summer__Position and direction_3_Describe position – forwards and backwards

title: The Left vs. Right Song! | Scratch Garden
ss_wr_desc: Introduce terms "left" and "right", using tools like rhymes, the "L" shape with the left hand, and writing hand for memory aid. Engage with games, songs, and daily instructions to reinforce these directions. Teach children to describe object positions and movement directions in relation to left or right.
small_step_id: Year 1_5-6_Summer__Position and direction_2_Describe position – left and right

title: The Money Song | UK Coins Song | Scratch Garden
ss_wr_desc: Children learn the value of different coin denominations, understanding that a 20p coin equals twenty 1p coins or two 10p coins. They explore why we use coins of varying values instead of only pennies. Once confident with pence, they're introduced to £1 and £2 coins, noting £1 equals 100p.

title: What Time Is It, Mr. Crocodile?- Read Aloud | Judy Sierra
ss_wr_desc: Introduce children to time-related vocabulary through daily routines and visual timetables. Encourage use of terms like "before", "after", "first", "next", "finally", "morning", "afternoon", "evening" to describe and order events. Utilise storybooks to contextualise these concepts in different scenarios.
small_step_id: Year 1_5-6_Summer__Time_1_Before and after, preposition time words

title: How Heavy - Kid's Math Storytime Read Aloud
ss_wr_desc: In this unit, children learn about mass, comparing objects' heaviness or lightness through touch and balance scales. They'll understand that heavier objects sit lower on scales, and explore misconceptions about size and shape affecting mass, using examples like balloons and modelling clay.
